subject: SLA breach: request pileup causing p99 token latency spikes
messages:
From: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: High p99 spikes across production (possible request pileup)

Rafael,

We started seeing elevated p99 token latencies around 15:10 PST today. The attached dump includes a sample of request IDs and timestamps where the latency jumped from ~200ms to >6s. This is impacting Checkout flows for several of our customers.

Quick summary:
- Window: 14:50–15:30 PST
- Impact: 12% of requests hit p99 > 5s, error rate up 0.8%
- Traffic: sustained peak but not dramatically higher than yesterday

Can Redwood confirm if there was any throttling, concurrency caps kicked, or if the platform applied any fallback variants? We need this triaged asap — we are at risk of missing our SLA.

Attached: request_dump_20270227.json, sla_dashboard_snapshot.png

Thanks,
Alex Dupree
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightLane AI

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p99 spikes across production (possible request pileup)

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. I'm escalating to on-call and looping in our infra and sales ops leads.

Immediate plan:
- Laura will triage KV cache and request routing traces to rule out prefix-queueing or backpressure from long-running streams.
- If we confirm concurrency cap enforcement, we'll propose a temporary uplift for BrightLane's pool and document expected cost.
- I'll keep you updated every hour until we have a root cause.

Can you confirm whether those request IDs are all to the same model version and if any clients saw 429s? That will help narrow routing vs runtime.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p99 spikes across production (possible request pileup)

Thanks Alex — I pulled the traces for the request IDs in request_dump_20270227.json. Early observations:
- Several long-tail traces show concurrent KV cache misses and one hotspot shard hitting GC pauses on the node that was serving BrightLane at that time.
- There's evidence of request pileup behind a slot allocation boundary: many requests queued waiting for a freed execution slot, producing the >5s tail.
- No systematic 429s in the sample; retries amplified the pileup.

Temporary mitigations I recommend while we fix the shard instability:
1) Increase BrightLane's concurrency cap by 30% for the next 4 hours (manual uplift).
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching on the affected model variant (reduces KV misses).
3) Route a small % (5%) to a compatible fallback GPU pool with warm caches.

I'll prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) with timings and cost impact. Rafael — if you can OK the uplift, my team can run it immediately.

Laura Bennett
Engineering PM, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 02:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p99 spikes across production (possible request pileup)

Rafael — appreciate the quick triage. Unfortunately the incident continued overnight and our SLA dashboard shows a breach window between 23:45–01:10 PST where p99 crossed the contractual threshold for two 15-min buckets. Our ops team is requesting a formal credit and immediate steps to avoid recurrence.

Relevant links: https://brightlane.example.com/sla/BL-3472/violations
We need:
- A MAP with timelines for permanent fix and mitigations
- Confirmation of any credits (scope & amount) and process
- A call with your execs to review SLA exposure

Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: BrightLane BL-3472 SLA breach — requesting leadership approval for immediate mitigations and credit

Team — BrightLane's production hit a contractual SLA breach overnight (see Alex's note). Laura proposes an immediate temporary uplift and routing to fallback pool to arrest the tail. Alex has asked for a MAP and confirmation of credits.

Proposed immediate actions (need approvals):
- Approve a 4-hour concurrency uplift for BrightLane (estimated incremental cost $1,400) — requires finance sign-off for ad-hoc credit acceptance.
- Approve credit steps: provisional 10% service credit for the breach window, to be finalized after postmortem.
- Schedule an emergency call with BrightLane and our execs at 10:30 PST to align on MAP and next steps.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (draft), sla_dashboard_snapshot.png

Alex — we will share the MAP and confirm credit process on the 10:30 call. Neha/Sean, please advise if I should route the credit to the standard finance credit flow or apply a special executive approval.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: BrightLane BL-3472 SLA breach — request leadership approval for mitigations and credit

Rafael — approve the temporary 4-hour concurrency uplift immediately. Also approve provisional 10% service credit for the impacted window; we'll finalize after postmortem and finance reconciliation.

I will:
- Open an expedited credit request with Finance and flag it as priority for BL-3472.
- Join the 10:30 PST call and provide a DocuSign link for the credit acknowledgement if BrightLane accepts provisional terms.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
